## Historical audit — S0344

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_31294395/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines. The supplied observations contain image paths, not the images themselves.

**Goal versus evidence:** The requested goal was a photo-matched indoor scene with separate editable meshes, camera, materials and lighting (line 1, `model_request`). The student interpreted the reference as a historic bedroom; that interpretation and its estimated bounds are not independent verification of the photograph (line 3, H `model_response`).

| Event | Observed evidence |
|---|---|
| Initial construction | H produced a complete program with architecture, two windows, bed, upholstered chair, screen, table, cabinet, pictures and rugs. Named assets contain child parts; chair parts were separate ellipsoids, and windows were shallow overlays rather than cut openings. The program specified colors, attempted procedural wallpaper, camera and two area lights (lines 3–4). This establishes emitted structure, not accurate physical connections or appearance. |
| First validation | Build and render completed, and step 1 was selected (lines 6, 8–10). The printed window-corner projection was approximately `(0.282, 0.234)` against the student’s estimated `(0.23, 0.08)` (line 9, `execution_result`). Projections are not visible-contour checks. |
| Revision and exploration | After receiving the reference, render and comparison instruction (line 11), H reported excessive room shell/floor, a too-small bed, and detached-looking chair arms. It changed camera position, target and lens 34→47; moved the chair, enlarged the bed, lowered its footboard, revised chair overlap, and added a small wooden chair (lines 13–14). The step-2 build and render completed (lines 16, 18–20). A numerical upward-aim trial moved landmark projections downward; the selected camera still left substantial point discrepancies (line 19). These visual diagnoses are H’s reports, not independently inspected images. |
| Final revision | H reported the second bed orientation and screen occlusion as wrong, then changed the bed’s long axis from Y to X, raised the screen, narrowed the chair, lowered the camera target, and adjusted colors (lines 23–24). A downward-aim trial moved selected projections upward; final projected bed-foot and chair points remained different from estimated reference points (line 29). Step 3 built and rendered successfully and was selected (lines 26, 28–30). No subsequent visual review is recorded. |

**Teacher input and autonomy:** No separate teacher message, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-directed execution is visible. The original task and runner’s repeated comparison instructions were received; the student’s subsequent reviews and revisions show use of that feedback format, not receipt of a separate teacher intervention. Sessions report no observable tool calls; the three Blender executions were runner events (lines 2, 12, 22; lines 4, 14, 24).

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Formal execution succeeded three times; final image-matching correctness is **unknown**, not established success. There is no visible technical interruption or empty patch. The reference and final render cannot be independently inspected here, so object completeness, pose, actual part connections, wallpaper application, lighting, crop and final visual fidelity remain unresolved. Camera versus local-geometry causes are hypotheses, especially because revisions changed several variables together.

**Transferable lesson:** Separate point projections from rendered contours and test camera direction before interpreting a change. **Task-specific lesson:** This student’s reported bed orientation, chair continuity and screen visibility motivated the final edits; their correctness remains unverified.
